ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act (FTRA), as amended, and its Enforcement Decree; Commercial Act, Title III (Companies); Commercial Registration Act and its Enforcement Rules; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, Court Administration Office, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague members: notarize the registrar's signature and then obtain an apostille from the Apostille Section of the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA). Non-members: do not apostille; use consular legalization through the Korean Embassy/Consulate or the destination-state Embassy in Seoul after MOFA legalization. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Active Existence and Registered Particulars)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague members: court certification followed by MOFA apostille. Non-members: parallel consular legalization route through MOFA legalization and the destination-state consulate or Korean consulate. Apostille and consular legalization must never be sequenced together for the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (PoA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public, Ministry of Justice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague members: authenticate the notary's seal at the MOFA Apostille Section. Non-members: notarize, then MOFA legalization, then consular legalization at the destination embassy/consulate. This is the alternative consular chain; do not add an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (certified copy / notarized version)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and Korean Notary Public, filed with and stamped by the District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague members: apostille from MOFA after notarization. Non-members: consular legalization at the destination state's diplomatic post in Seoul or Korean consulate abroad; never both apostille and consular legalization for the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Korean foreign-exchange bank reference including LC track record)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The corporate customer's bank in Korea, e.g. KEB Hana Bank, Woori Bank, Shinhan Bank, or Industrial Bank of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague members: bank branch signature acknowledged and then apostilled via MOFA. Non-members: bank signature legalized through MOFA and the destination-state consulate; if the destination is a non-member state, bank officers may also sign before a notary to feed the consular legalization chain. The routes are alternative, not cumulative.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, signatory, beneficial owner, LC applicant, and payment counterparty must be screened at formation and continuously against KoFIU domestic terrorist and FTRA watchlists, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, including UNSCR 1718/2231/2616, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and worldwide PEP databases covering immediate family and close associates. Screening must verify 25% or control ownership using notarized shareholder registers and declaration of person with significant control; any nil, mismatched, or high-risk hit requires enhanced due diligence, independent negative news review, source-of-wealth and evidence-of-funds verification, and suspicious transaction reporting to KoFIU if unresolved. Re-screen at 12-month intervals and upon transaction trigger events, and incorporate tax transparency and FATF flag lists.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-Registry), the official electronic name-search and corporate registration portal operated by the Court Administration Office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name of a Chusik Hoesa must be in Hangeul; the name must include the legal-form element Chusik Hoesa, contain a distinctive Korean-language element, and may carry a Romanized transliteration in the Articles of Association for banking and LC use. The registry requires exact Korean characters; identical or confusingly similar names in the same registry jurisdiction are excluded, and foreign-language names must match the registered Hangeul name phonetically when used in bank documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Republic of Korea as standalone official title
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within two weeks of the written rejection, the representative must file a written objection with the same registration section claiming priority or non-identity; the registration officer reviews the objection and must issue a reasoned decision. If still rejected, the applicant may apply for a provisional order to cancel the name acceptance from the civil district court or file an administrative appeal with the competent court. After the appeal is decided, immediate re-filing under a revised name is permitted. Preserve every rejection notice, search screenshot, and appeal receipt for the AML file.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole statutory registered office for a Korean Chusik Hoesa engaging in bulk petrochemical polymer wholesale. The National Tax Service and district registration courts require a verifiable physical place of business under the Direct Control of the company where books and management are kept. A serviced-office address may be accepted only if there is a real leased desk, office signage, structured meeting space, dedicated mail handling, and a resident director or employee; however, most Korean foreign-exchange banks will reject or de-risk a virtual-office corporate client for LC-based petrochemical trading on anti-money-laundering and residence grounds. An actual registered office and warehouse-risk documentation are mandatory for KYC, VAT and corporate tax invoicing, and trade finance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified likelihood: Medium-High (estimated 45% in the first year) for newly registered wholesale traders under ISIC 4669 when the registered office is not owner-occupied. Checklist: verify exterior signage, registered office presence during business hours, original business registration certificate, tax invoices, lease contract, seating, IT and communication systems, attendance records, inventory and supply-chain contracts, LC and export-import declarations, bank debit records, and corporate seal custody. Any mismatch among address, utility invoice, employee census, and customs broker data will trigger an unannounced revisit and possible tax correction.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, December 14, 1962, as amended), particularly Articles 288 to 317 and 318; Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Distribution Industry Development Act and Fire Service Act for physical warehouse licensing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Civil Affairs Bureau, District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO/e-Ro)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporate Registration of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Korean Commercial Act sets no minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa; the amount of capital is fixed in the Articles of Incorporation and must be fully paid into a temporary incorporation bank account before registration. If the foreign investor remits KRW 100,000,000 or more and holds at least 10 percent voting ownership, an FDI report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act must be filed with a designated bank or KOTRA, which will issue a foreign investment certificate. For smaller remittances, a foreign exchange transaction report is sufficient. There is no blocked escrow account requirement; the subscribed capital is held in the temporary incorporation account and is released only after the incorporation registration certificate and business registration certificate are obtained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: at the first meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company], a Chusik Hoesa organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, held on [date] and duly noticed to all directors, the following resolutions are adopted. 1. Share Capital Subscription and Issuance. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company is [KRW] divided into [number] ordinary shares of par value [KRW] each; that the issue and allotment of [number] ordinary shares to the subscribers named in the subscription list for aggregate consideration of [KRW], fully paid in cash, is hereby ratified, approved and confirmed; that the directors are directed to keep the subscription proceeds in the corporate capital account of the Company with [Bank] and to issue share certificates in conformity with Articles 295, 302, 318 and 319 of the Commercial Act; and that no shares are issued below par and no fractional shares are created. 2. Banking Authorization and Payment Rails. RESOLVED, that [Bank] is designated as the principal depository bank of the Company; that the Representative Director and [second signatory] are authorized to open, operate, close and maintain deposit, foreign currency, payroll and treasury accounts; to sign checks, payment orders, foreign exchange contracts and electronic SWIFT instructions; and to accept, issue, endorse, discount and negotiate bills of exchange and letters of credit, including irrevocable documentary credits used for the purchase and wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules; that transactions exceeding a monthly aggregate of [KRW] require two authorized signatures, and ordinary operating expenses may be signed by one. 3. Registered Office Adoption. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company is fixed at [full address], Republic of Korea; that the corporate seal, statutory registers, books and records are kept at that address; that the Representative Director is authorized to execute the lease, pay rent and deposits, and to file any change of registered office with the competent District Court Registry within the statutory period; and that this resolution is sufficient corporate authorization for lessors, banks and government registers. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] is appointed Inside Director; and [Name] is appointed Statutory Auditor; each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until a successor is duly elected; that annual remuneration is fixed at [KRW] per officer; and that the Representative Director is directed to register the directors, auditor and corporate seal under Article 317 of the Commercial Act and to file all national tax and employment registrations. 5. Ratification and Implementation. RESOLVED, that all acts performed by the promoters and initial incorporators before this meeting, including subscription and payment for shares, notarization of the Articles of Incorporation, opening of the temporary capital account, and preparation of regulatory filings, are hereby ratified and confirmed; and that each officer is authorized to execute every document and do all things necessary to carry out these resolutions, with the Board reviewing compliance quarterly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment notification, company name availability search, and initial due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA One-Pass Foreign Investment Support Center; designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a signed foreign investment notification or FDI report to KOTRA or the designated bank at the foreign investor's address before remitting capital, stating the investor identity, investment amount, shareholding percentage, target business code ISIC 4669, and proposed Chusik Hoesa name. In parallel, conduct a company name availability search using the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) because the Commercial Registration Register reserves the trade name. If the foreign investor subscribes KRW 100 million or more, obtain a foreign investment certificate to facilitate capital remittance and subsequent registration. The receipt or certificate issued in this step must be retained and submitted to the notary and court registry. Any later change to the investment amount or business scope requires an amended report.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment notification/report form or FDI report form
Passport copy or corporate certificate of foreign investor
Power of attorney to resident officer/service agent
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Statement of investment purpose and securities subscription plan
Lease agreement or address evidence of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KOTRA or the designated bank rejects or returns the report for correction, submit the corrected statement within seven business days and request expedited re-indexing; no additional fee is payable if the correction does not change the business scope or investment amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of Articles of Incorporation and opening of temporary capital subscription account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public under the Notary Act; Korean commercial bank with incorporation-account service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must execute the Articles of Incorporation in Korean or with an official Korean translation and have the instrument notarized by a Korean notary public. The articles must contain the business purpose, trade name, number and par value of shares, registered office location, method of notice, and initial directors. The directors-elect and auditors must sign the subscription list or a written officers election consent. The promoters then open and deposit the full subscription price into a temporary incorporation account in the name of the future company at a commercial bank; the bank will issue a certificate of capital deposit which is a mandatory registration document. Funds in the account cannot be withdrawn until the company is registered and the corporate business account is opened. If any subscriber withdraws before registration, a new board consent or promoters resolution must be executed.
required_dossiers: Notarization request form
Executed Articles of Incorporation
Subscription list signed by each subscriber
Officers election consent
Bank temporary account opening application and anti-money-laundering forms
Certificate of capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal defect, revise the articles and resubmit for certification; if the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, provide certified passports, source-of-funds evidence, and the foreign investment certificate from KOTRA, and resubmit within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing incorporation registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Civil Affairs Bureau, District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office; online via Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fourteen days after the full share subscription price is deposited, the directors-elect must file the stock company incorporation application with the competent District Court Registry. The filing includes the court-prescribed registration form, notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of capital deposit, subscription list, minutes of incorporation meeting or written consent of officers, report on shares allotted, and lawful seal registration. The applicant pays the court registration tax and local education surtax; the exact amount is computed by the registry fee schedule from paid-in capital and number of shares. The registry will examine formal compliance and issue an incorporation registration certificate and certified commercial register extract. The Chusik Hoesa comes into existence as a separate legal entity only on the date of this registration, so the certificate must be checked for exact entity name, address and officers before any contract or license application is made.
required_dossiers: Application for commercial registration in the form prescribed by the Supreme Court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of payment of share issue price
Subscription list signed by subscribers
Minutes of incorporation meeting or written consent of directors and auditor
Report on number of shares issued and capital amount
Corporate seal registration application
Power of attorney or notarized resolution for foreign directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementation order, submit the missing documents within fourteen days through the IRO or in person; if the statutory suspension period expires, file a new application and pay the registration tax again, and request a priority review with a written explanation of the earlier docket number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service and activation of the corporate operating bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the principal office; HomeTax System online portal; designated commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after incorporation, file the business registration application with the supervising district tax office, attaching the court registration certificate, certified Articles of Incorporation, corporate seal certificate, and identity documents of the Representative Director. Request issuance of the business registration certificate and tax invoice or electronic tax invoice certificates for value-added tax, corporate tax, and employee withholding returns. After obtaining the business registration certificate, open the company operating bank account at [Bank], present the business registration certificate, court registration extract, corporate seal certificate, board resolution on banking authorization, and beneficial ownership declarations, and activate SWIFT and letter-of-credit services for wholesale petrochemical polymer payments. The temporary incorporation capital account may then be closed and the capital balance transferred to the operating account.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Court incorporation registration certificate
Certified copy of Commercial Register
Corporate seal certificate
Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of Representative Director
Bank account application forms and beneficial ownership declarations
Board resolution on banking authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests beneficial ownership evidence, submit the shareholder register and passports within ten days; if the bank holds automated compliance, submit the corporate resolution and risk questionnaire and re-apply; late business registration is subject to NTS penalty after twenty days, so use expedited online filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration physical and environmental licensing and civil-defense or fire-safety clearance for warehousing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal government; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA); National Fire Agency through the local fire station; Ministry of Environment and Korea Environment Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For pure wholesale trading without any storage, no industrial operating license is required. If the Chusik Hoesa maintains a physical warehouse for polyethylene and polypropylene granules, obtain a building use or warehouse occupancy approval from the local Si/Gun/Gu office in accordance with the Building Act; submit the safety and health initiation report to KOSHA under the Occupational Safety and Health Act; apply for fire system installation and fire safety inspection approval from the local fire station before the warehouse is occupied; and determine whether a Small-Scale Environmental Impact Review is required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act for a floor area exceeding 5,000 square meters or a project in a protected or prescribed management area. The company must keep material safety data sheets and polymer handling procedures at the site. All licenses must be in place before physical operations begin.
required_dossiers: Building permit or warehouse occupancy approval
KOSHA safety and health initiation report
Fire system installation and completion inspection application
Fire equipment layout drawings
Small-Scale Environmental Impact Review report and approval decision, if triggered
Material safety data sheets for polymer supplies
Waste storage and disposal documentation, if waste is generated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If approval is conditioned or refused, address each condition in writing and request re-inspection within thirty days; fire correction orders may be appealed through administrative review before the Ministry of the Interior and Safety; do not commence physical operations until all clearance certificates, including the fire safety completion certificate, are issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL) and Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA); local Si/Gun/Gu municipal government; National Fire Agency through the local fire station
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License under the Value-Added Tax Act; Warehouse or Occupancy Approval under the Building Act; KOSHA Safety and Health Initiation Report under the Occupational Safety and Health Act; Fire Safety Completion Certificate under the Fire Service Act; Chemical Substances Handling Report under the Chemical Substances Control Act only if any inventory is classified as a controlled chemical, which virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules generally are not

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE); Korea Environment Corporation (K-eco); local Si/Gun/Gu environmental department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Wholesale trading of virgin PE/PP granules is not a full Environmental Impact Assessment activity by itself. A Small-Scale Environmental Impact Review (SSEIR) under Article 43 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is triggered when the storage or warehouse floor area is 5,000 square meters or more, or when the project is located in an environmentally protected or conservation management area designated by local land-use zoning. For smaller non-sensitive warehouses, an environmental registration or a finding of no EIA is sufficient; compliance with waste and water statutes remains mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or process VOC exhaust is generated during bagged or pellet storage, so the site is treated as a warehouse. If floor wash water, cooling water or stormwater is discharged to public waters, MOE general wastewater standards apply: BOD 30 mg/L, COD 40 mg/L, SS 30 mg/L, total nitrogen 60 mg/L, and total phosphorus 8 mg/L. If a baghouse or ventilation stack is installed for transfer dust, total particulate concentration must not exceed 30 mg/Sm3 under the Clean Air Conservation Act. Fugitive dust at the warehouse boundary must be controlled by wet suppression or filters. Virgin polymer is not hazardous waste; contaminated or off-spec polymer intended for disposal must be characterized under the Waste Control Act, transported by a licensed waste handler if hazardous, and stored on site for no more than thirty days without a waste storage permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety System Approval and Completion Inspection under the Fire Service Act must be obtained before warehouse occupancy; automatic fire alarm, extinguishers, hydrants and emergency exit lighting are mandatory based on storage floor area. A structural load and racking safety certification prepared by a licensed structural engineer is required for high-bay racking. The company must file an Occupational Safety and Health initiation report with KOSHA, complete workplace risk assessments, provide personal protective equipment and first aid, and conduct fire drills. No separate civil defense shelter approval is required for a general warehouse unless the local ordinance classifies the building as a civil defense facility; if so, a structural civil defense shelter permit must be obtained from the local government before operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, an external bureau of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, operating the HomeTax online electronic tax portal (hometax.go.kr); customs export clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNIPASS electronic trade single window (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation, the Korean Chusik Hoesa must file a Business Registration Application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over its principal place of business within 20 days of business commencement pursuant to Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act; the filing may be made electronically through HomeTax or in person and must be supported by the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, shareholder registry, lease or title evidence for the domestic place of business, and, where the board is controlled by foreign non-resident shareholders, a power of attorney designating the Korean tax representative; the district tax office then issues the unified 10-digit Business Registration Number, which constitutes the single statutory Tax Identification Number for corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding tax purposes. For a foreign non-resident corporation without a domestic place of business, the foreign entity must separately register through its appointed Korean tax representative with the Seoul Regional Tax Office to obtain a VAT registration and withholding account. fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting as the central bank and foreign exchange oversight authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the policy-setter for FX and capital transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains an open but regulated current-account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations. Ordinary trade- and service-related remittances are freely convertible through authorized foreign exchange banks. Capital-account transactions operate on a positive-list and reporting basis: direct foreign investment, intercompany loans, cross-border guarantees, and derivative transactions are permitted when filed or approved under the FETA. The Korean won is domestically fully usable but cannot be circulated offshore in unrestricted volume; an offshore non-deliverable market exists, while onshore KRW conversion must be executed through banks under the real-name transaction system and reported via the BOK-managed Foreign Exchange Information System. Export proceeds must be collected through a Korean authorized bank and either retained in a foreign-currency account or converted into KRW, creating a transparent audit trail. Profit remittance hurdles for a Chusik Hoesa are present but manageable: the company must maintain an active foreign-invested company registration with KOTRA/Invest Korea, file verified financial statements, settle applicable Korean corporate and withholding taxes, and present board minutes confirming dividends together with the bank's underlying FX settlement report. Each outgoing dividend must pass independent source-of-funds and sanctions screening before remittance. Liquidation proceeds are repatriable after tax clearance and cancellation of the foreign-investor registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA, export proceeds must be received within 18 months from the date of export declaration unless an extension is approved by MOEF. Once received, the foreign currency must be deposited without undue delay into a foreign-currency account at an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank or sold to that bank. There is no mandatory percentage conversion into KRW; the effective mandatory conversion ratio is 0%, and the exporter may hold the proceeds in foreign currency. However, when conversion is needed, it must be executed through the authorized bank, marked with the appropriate trade settlement purpose code, and the export settlement must be reported in the BOK trade settlement statistics. Failure to meet the statutory receipt deadline creates customs enforcement and documentary penalty exposure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investor Deposit Account (Capital Escrow) and KRW Corporate Operating Account
KRW Corporate Current Account and Managed Foreign Currency Account (USD/JPY/EUR)
Corporate Settlement Account with Trade Finance and LC Desk
Trade-Focused Irrevocable LC Settlement Account and FX Hedging Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a principal onshore treasury rail. An offshore fintech EMI is not automatically barred from invoicing or ancillary payments to Korean counterparties, but it cannot open a domestic KRW current account, cannot provide Korean electronic settlement instructions, and is not recognized as a foreign exchange business operator under FETA. Korean Tier-1 banks will not accept EMI accounts for statutory foreign-investment capital verification or FX reporting. For a bulk petrochemical trading Chusik Hoesa, use of a fintech EMI is limited to peripheral multi-currency cash concentration outside Korea; all regulated KRW, trade finance, LC, and FX hedging must pass through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is the default and normally mandatory for the representative director (statutory director) and for any natural person holding 10% or more of the Chusik Hoesa through the ultimate beneficial ownership chain. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard product in Korea; it is accepted only in rare, bank-specific cases and never for the first enhanced-risk account of a newly formed petrochemical commodity trading vehicle. Korean banks will in practice require the foreign UBO or the registered in-country director to attend an interview at the domestic HQ branch, present a valid passport or Alien Registration Card, and sign the real-name transaction agreement. Power-of-attorney arrangements must be notarized in the home country, apostilled under the Hague Convention or consular legalized, and then approved by the bank's AML committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee and shell holding opacity above the 25% UBO threshold; the bank cannot identify the natural persons controlling the Korean trade vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership diagram, notarized UBO declarations for every natural person, corporate registry extracts from all holding jurisdictions (with apostille), nominee disclaimers signed by holding companies, tax residence certificates, and transaction history for the remitting parent for the past 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering typology: over- or under-invoicing of homogeneous polyethylene and polypropylene pellets relative to published market prices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent commodity price benchmark screens (ICIS/Platts/S&P Global), entire contractual chain from producer to the Korean entity, signed purchase orders and sales contracts, LC/telex copies, bills of lading, warehouse receipts, terminal/tolling weighbridge certificates, marine insurance certificates, and Korea Customs import declarations showing reconciliation of quantity and arm's-length unit price.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large injection of FDI capital from a high-risk jurisdiction or from a jurisdiction with weak AML supervision into a single limited liability vehicle with no operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements for the originating account, MT103 SWIFT confirmation, source-of-wealth file for the investing shareholder, audited financial statements of the foreign investor, corporate commercial purpose memo, supply contracts covering the petrochemical bulk flow, and evidence that the funds are not layered through multiple offshore intermediaries within 24 hours.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and rapid outbound disbursements shortly after capitalization, inconsistent with the stated import cycle and indicating possible money pass-through or trade-based laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward 12-month treasury and purchase plan, board-approved delegation matrix, executed supplier contracts with projected drawdown dates, inventory or landed-cost schedules, LC limits, USD/KRW hedging requirements, and a written liquidity management policy showing separate operating, trade settlement, and FX margin accounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for a foreign investor establishing a Korean Chusik Hoesa: (1) open a Foreign Investor Deposit Account with a Tier-1 authorized foreign exchange bank in the name of the foreign investor; (2) remit paid-in capital via SWIFT MT103 using the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code for direct equity investment in a domestic corporation; (3) the bank credits the Foreign Investor Deposit Account and the investor submits a Foreign Investment Report through KOTRA/Invest Korea or the bank before or within the statutory window; (4) after the bank issues the Foreign Investment Confirmation Certificate, the investor incorporates the Chusik Hoesa at the relevant Korean Commercial Court registry; (5) transfer the verified investment funds from the escrow-type deposit account into the corporation's KRW operating account and, for capital verification, retain the deposit certificate, foreign investment certificate, bank receipt, and corporate registration certificate in the treasury records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT-based documentary credit as the primary rail. The Korean corporate bank opens an irrevocable documentary L/C via SWIFT MT700 in favor of the overseas polymer producer for each bulk import lot. Settlement on presentation of UCP600-compliant documents is executed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 through the bank's clearing channel. For smaller or repeated contracts, documents against payment (DP) and documents against acceptance (DA) collections are permitted. All outbound disbursements must align with Korea Customs import declarations and be booked against the authorized FX settlement code; any KRW conversion requires a foreign exchange transaction report. Open-account payments to trusted suppliers are acceptable after credit approval but should be governed by annual LC/revolving trade limits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Trade-related deliverable KRW/USD forward and swap contracts executed with an authorized Tier-1 Korean bank, at a notional capped at 100% of underlying verified trade invoices and with settlement matched to the import/export payment date.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/KRW) used solely to hedge currency risk on trade finance liabilities or major capital expenditures, with maturity not exceeding the underlying facility tenure and requiring board-approved hedging policy.
Outright FX options purchased (not written) for commodity trade exposures, limited to an explicit premium budget and subject to the bank's derivative eligibility assessment.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): not permissible as a primary onshore hedge for a Chusik Hoesa; any attempted onshore NDF must be rejected as outside the Korean resident exemption framework, while non-resident counterparties may continue to price the KRW NDF offshore.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders: presentation and approval of balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, business report, and appropriation/re-disposal of retained earnings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a filing; corporate records maintained at the registered office and records filed as part of the subsequent court registration filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December year-end, by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene an annual general meeting is subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Commercial Act; unresolved approval does not suspend the court registration obligation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Court filing of the approved financial statements and the annual general meeting resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Court of Registration / Registration Office of the Local District Court (Supreme Court registry system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the annual general meeting approves the financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within 15 days triggers a negligence fine under the Commercial Act (up to KRW 5,000,000) and the company is exposed to de facto inability to file registrable changes; continuous non-compliance may be prosecuted as a registration duty violation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return including tax-reconciliation schedules, book financial statements, and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the Hometax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December fiscal year-end: by March 31 of the following fiscal year; for a different fiscal year, within three months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A non-filing or under-declaration penalty of 20% of the tax payable is imposed; an insufficient payment additionally accrues 0.022% per day of delinquency; continued refusal to file can lead to tax authorities' forced assessment and collection, and a criminal fine under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return (the regional component of corporate income tax / local income tax surcharge)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (municipal or provincial authority) via the WeTax local taxation e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year, aligned with the corporate income tax return due date; for a December year-end, by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underpayment attracts an additional tax of 10% to 20% of the unpaid local tax amount and a daily overdue charge of 0.75% per month up to 36 months under the Framework Act on Local Taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual reporting of a foreign-invested company's current capital stock, shareholding status, foreign investors, and operating performance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), through the Korea Investment Ombudsman's Integrated System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year, unless a change report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act has already been filed; material share-transfer events require a separate report within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in revocation of foreign-investment registration and loss of tax exemptions/customs privileges, plus an administrative fine for negligence under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; repeated non-reporting can invalidate foreign-investor rights in repatriation approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified-PA audit report and audited financial statements (only if the statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART electronic disclosure, with the audit report simultaneously delivered to the National Tax Service on approval of the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent audit must be completed and the audit report submitted to the shareholders and the FSS before the annual general meeting; audited financial statements must be filed with the FSS and registry within 15 days after the general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or submit the audit report without reasonable cause subjects the company and responsible directors to sanctions under the External Audit Act, including fines up to KRW 50,000,000, external-audit acts leading to FSS inspection, notification of non-audited status, and revocation of listing or registration advantages.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa is legally subject to independent certified-CPA audit if it is listed on a Korean securities exchange, or if, as at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, its total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000 at normal exchange reference); in addition, the Financial Services Commission may designate a company as subject-to-audit where the company applies K-IFRS, is a financial institution, or is otherwise designated for public-interest reasons. Korea does not apply a simple turnover-only statutory audit trigger for private wholesale companies; headcount alone is not an independent external-audit trigger, but total assets is the decisive balance-sheet threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for all companies subject to statutory external audit; non-audit-subject private companies may apply Korean GAAP / Korean SMEs Accounting Standards (K-SME GAAP) for financial statements submitted in the statutory tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Chusik Hoesa must maintain its shareholder register at the registered office and record all transfers, pledges, rights suspensions, and cancellations without delay. For any change of a 25%+ ultimate beneficial owner or any foreign-investor shareholding event, the company must update the register within 30 days and, if it is a foreign-invested company, file the prescribed change report with MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days. Once a year, the shareholder register must be reconciled against the foreign-investment report, and the annual foreign-investment current-status report must be filed by the statutory deadline; failure to perform this annual confirmation exposes the company to foreign-investment deregistration and municipal/tax penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Statutory Auditors and Audit Committee Members
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board of Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 2,500 per annum for a Korean corporate/registered agent or in-country corporate secretarial retainer
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 45,000 per annum for an independent CPA audit of a medium-sized petrochemical wholesale distribution company, depending on transaction volume, inventory/LC flows, and group reporting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% central headline rate (10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on the next tranche; 22% on the excess), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge, producing a top combined rate of 24.2%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, qualifying foreign-invested enterprises in Foreign Investment Zones and Free Economic Zones can receive 100% corporate income tax exemption for up to 5 years and a 50% reduction for the following 2 years; technology-intensive R&D expenditures generate tax credits or super-deductions of 20%-50%; income from qualified patented technology transfers may be reduced to a 10% rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return - Form No. 1 (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) and accompanying schedules, filed through the National Tax Service HomeTaxes (HTS) electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (final return) plus statutory half-year interim prepayment return for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (31 March for calendar-year entities); one additional month is available when the return is prepared by a certified tax accountant; foreign corporations with a Korean permanent establishment have the same annual filing obligation and must also comply with DTA withholding certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, registration number, business year, head office address, principal industry code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List direct and ultimate non-resident shareholders with residency country and shareholding percentage; attach evidence that the Chusik Hoesa's effective management is in Korea and, if applicable, branch or PE registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Gross revenue and sales adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and income from wholesale of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules, including LC and foreign-exchange adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate cross-border revenue under a functional analysis; do not include offshore affiliate profits in Korean revenue; attach arm's-length documentation if related-party revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable income after statutory adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income after deductible expenses, depreciation, inventory valuation, bad debt, and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only properly sourced and documented intercompany costs; 22% WHT must be withheld on royalties and interest paid to non-residents before claiming deductions; transfer pricing adjustments are mandatory when margins deviate from the arm's-length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax base and loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income less loss carryforward, non-taxable income, and special deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include CFC income of offshore subsidiaries and deemed dividends; treaty-derived income eligible for foreign tax credits must be scheduled separately with residency certificates and beneficial ownership support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax calculated and local surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive statutory rates and 10% local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute foreign tax credit limitation separately by source country; do not use excess foreign tax credits beyond the Korean residual tax; attach DTA relief applications for outbound payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Prepayments, credits, and net tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct interim payments, advance payments, and withholding taxes; report final balance payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If excess WHT was withheld in a prior year, file a tax appeal or refund claim before the statutory deadline; underpaid balances accrue daily penalties; directors should ensure liquidity to avoid personal secondary collection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline subjects the taxpayer to an additional tax of 20% of the tax payable (or 10% for an unfaithful understated return; 40% for fraudulently under-reported taxes) under the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus daily delinquency interest on the unpaid amount until full payment. The National Tax Service may impose estimated assessment, seizure, asset freeze, travel ban, and public name disclosure. Fraudulent evasion is referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, Article 3, punishable by imprisonment with labor up to 2 years or a fine up to twice the evaded tax; large-amount evasion above the statutory aggravated threshold may trigger a minimum imprisonment term; controlling directors may be jointly and severally liable through veil-piercing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% corporate-income-tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge), before application of a bilateral DTA
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The withholding agent must obtain the non-resident shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence country's tax authority, a fully executed beneficial ownership declaration, evidence that the recipient is not an agent, nominee, or conduit, proof of satisfaction of the limitation-on-benefits clause, and the underlying dividend resolution or payment documents. The application for reduced withholding must be filed with the appropriate district tax office before the payment date; if the reduced rate is not applied in time, a refund or reassessment claim must be filed within the statutory time limit, and the NTS may deny relief if the recipient is not the beneficial owner or fails the treaty anti-abuse test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are also 22% (20% plus 2%) for interest on intercompany debt and royalties on industrial, commercial, or scientific IP. Treaty rates under OECD-pattern DTAs typically range from 0% to 10% for interest and 10% to 15% for royalties, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and the amount is at arm's length.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in aggregate cross-border transactions with specially related parties for Master File/Local File preparation; KRW 1 trillion group consolidated revenue for Country-by-Country Report preparation; contemporaneous TP documentation may be required earlier upon examination order.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not administer a separate ESR filing regime, but the OECD substance standard is implemented through the Act for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and judicial substance-over-form analysis. A Chusik Hoesa must perform its Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea through employees, management decisions, office premises, and risk-bearing capacity. If a foreign-owned Korean entity is found to be a shell lacking real decision-making, the NTS may disregard its separate existence and attribute trading income to the actual foreign principal; CFC rules similarly attribute low-taxed passive income to Korean shareholders. This is the functional Korean analogue to ESR and the CIGA analysis.
